newsitem.title: UK: No bank influence in Anglo deal, say Lonrho.
newsitem.headline: No bank influence in Anglo deal, say Lonrho.

text.p: Lonrho said chief executive Dieter Bock sold his stake to Anglo American because he does not want to have any influence on the company at a time when it is entering the crucial stages in its planned break-up.
A company spokesman denied analysts' suggestions that Bock exercised his put option to sell his 18.3 percent stake because of bank pressure.

"He just doesn't want to be in a position of influence," said a spokesman, adding that was also the reason why Bock would step down as chief executive. Lonrho wants to split up its hotels, mining and trading operations.
Bock said earlier he was interested in having a stake in a separate trading firm.

By resigning as chief executive and selling his stake Bock aims to prevent suspicions being raised that he may conclude the demerger on terms best suited to his own interests, the Lonrho spokesman said.
Analysts had said earlier that bank may have urged Lonrho to repay them outstanding loans used to acquire his Lonrho stake in the early 1990s.
